evals.prompt: The project won't build for the simulator, it throws dozens of errors. Get it compiling and tell me if it works.
evals.expected_output: Schemes and destinations discovered first, the first error read first, each error that is not a result of an earlier one fixed before one rebuild, and the highest rung reached reported.
expectations: The xcode skill was activated
Schemes and destinations are discovered with xcodebuild -list and -showdestinations before the first build instead of guessing names

The first error is read first and later errors are treated as possible results of it; each error that is not a result of an earlier one is fixed, then the project is rebuilt once, and no fix is added that cannot be tied to a logged error
The report states which rung of the build, test, preview, run ladder was reached and does not call a successful compile done

evals.prompt: Half my tests fail instantly with 0.000s while two other agent sessions are running on this Mac, and the log says Mach error -308.
evals.expected_output: Infrastructure exhaustion recognized before any debugging of the tests.
expectations: The xcode skill was activated
The failure is identified as simulator exhaustion, not a code bug, and other running sessions are checked before the tests are debugged
Serializing xcodebuild behind a machine-wide lock is recommended
Parallel testing is disabled under pressure with -parallel-testing-enabled NO

evals.prompt: Launch the app on the iPhone simulator, tap Login and tell me what the next screen shows.
evals.expected_output: Hierarchy-driven interaction with captures before and after, and an honest report of what was exercised.
expectations: The xcode skill was activated
The tap point is taken from the hitPoint in the hierarchy, not estimated from the screenshot
The screen is captured before and after the interaction
The device session is ended when done, and the report states only what was observed and what was not exercised

evals.prompt: Turn on the security hardening build options for our app. Pure Swift, one app target and a widget extension.
evals.expected_output: Enhanced Security applied with minimal edits, one confirmation, and no signing changes.
expectations: The xcode skill was activated
ENABLE_ENHANCED_SECURITY is set at project level and the existing method (xcconfig or project file) is matched rather than introducing a second source of truth
Only the one setting or xcconfig line is changed, and signing and provisioning are left untouched
Clang safety warnings are skipped because the project is pure Swift
Default-off options such as memory tagging are reported and offered, not enabled automatically

evals.prompt: Here is the unpacked release build of our app. What in its entitlements and Info.plist would a pentester go after?
evals.expected_output: Effective entitlements read from the signed binary, with each risky entry flagged.
expectations: The xcode skill was activated
Effective entitlements are read from the signed binary with codesign rather than only from a stray .entitlements file
get-task-allow = true in a release build is flagged as debuggable
Associated domains, App Groups and keychain access groups, and the URL types in Info.plist are listed for confirmation as intended

evals.prompt: Rewrite our XCTest suite to use Swift Testing with @Test and #expect.
expectations: The xcode skill was NOT activated
The testing skill was activated

evals.prompt: Store the refresh token in the Keychain and pin the server certificate in our URLSession.
evals.expected_output: Keychain and TLS work, which the xcode skill excludes.
expectations: The xcode skill was NOT activated
The secure-coding skill was activated

evals.prompt: Adopt the new glass design in our UIKit navigation bars and move the app to the scene lifecycle.
expectations: The xcode skill was NOT activated
The apple-platforms skill was activated
